title: Pangenome-guided breeding restores high-altitude adaptation and improves yield in Tartary buckwheat.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran paper_context.py: not open access, no PMCID, no full text, no supplement, no NCBI links (GEO/SRA/BioProject), no Zenodo/Dryad hit on the DOI; only antibody RRIDs text-mined. One web search found news coverage but no data repository accession or phenotype table.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: 16-accession pangenome, 123,131 structural variants, telomere-to-telomere reference (abstract). News coverage says genetic data from 994 accessions across 15 countries were integrated and that Tables S1-S4 exist; none of this was seen as files.

a1_downloadable.note: No repository accession found anywhere (no NCBI links, no Zenodo/Dryad, no full text). Assemblies and reads are likely in China's CNCB/GSA, but unconfirmed; any phenotype table is in a paywalled supplement.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: No per-accession phenotype table (seed size, altitude adaptation) was located; a label would have to be assembled from paywalled supplements and possibly earlier resequencing papers. Checked: nothing found; paper not readable.

a3_inputs_present.note: Genotypes would come from raw resequencing reads or assemblies requiring variant calling; no processed variant matrix located.

a4_units_stated.note: No phenotype file seen, so units unknown.

a5_enough_rows.note: The pangenome itself is 16 accessions, far too few. A 994-accession panel is mentioned in news only; phenotype counts for it unverified.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: unknown; likely tens to hundreds of GB of reads/assemblies
a6_fits_laptop.note: Building a genotype matrix from raw data for ~1,000 accessions exceeds a laptop's practical budget.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No files to compare against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: Seed size and field yield would be physical measurements, if a table existed; not verified.

backbone.name: none checked; plant DNA language models (e.g. AgroNT) would be the candidate

controls.positive_control: FtPLATZ copy number / 28-bp promoter insertion should predict seed size (paper's claim).

honest_claim_h3: At best: predicts seed size from genotype among the Tartary buckwheat accessions this group sequenced and phenotyped, if such a table were released.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA variants of buckwheat varieties to predict their seed size and high-altitude performance.
plain_idea.train_on: Genotypes (structural and point variants) of buckwheat accessions; 16 in the pangenome, a 994-accession panel mentioned in press coverage only, so usable count unknown.
plain_idea.predict: Seed size or yield per accession, measured in field trials, if the per-accession phenotype table were public.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Breeders choosing parents for Himalayan buckwheat could screen lines by genotype instead of multi-season field trials.

ml_idea: Genomic prediction of seed size from a ~1,000-accession genotype panel; not feasible without a located phenotype table and processed genotype matrix.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: no data files located.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Find the paper's data availability statement (GSA/BioProject IDs) and check whether a per-accession phenotype table for the 994 accessions is downloadable.

verdict_reason: Paywalled paper with no located data: no accessions, no supplement, no phenotype table. The pangenome is 16 genomes, and any larger panel would need variant calling from raw reads plus an unseen phenotype table (fails A1, A2, A5, A6).
